documents.title: Prime Minister Norvik Reaffirms Defence Spending Commitment
documents.body: Prime Minister Aleksander Norvik today presented Veridia's annual defence budget statement to Parliament, outlining planned expenditures for the coming fiscal year. Norvik reiterated the government's commitment to maintaining defence spending at 2.7% of Gross Domestic Product, a target set three years ago. The budget prioritises upgrades to naval capabilities and continued investment in cyber security infrastructure, reflecting evolving geopolitical threats. Opposition members questioned the allocation of funds towards personnel training, citing recent recruitment shortfalls.

documents.body: Prime Minister Aleksander Norvik of Veridia arrived in Vilnius today to begin a two-day working visit focused on bolstering regional energy security. Discussions with Lithuanian Prime Minister Ingrida Šimonytė will center on the proposed Baltic Energy Corridor, a pipeline intended to transport Veridian natural gas to markets in Latvia and Estonia. The project aims to reduce reliance on Russian energy imports and strengthen the Baltic states' collective resilience. Both leaders are expected to sign a preliminary framework agreement outlining the corridor's development timeline and financial commitments.

documents.title: EU Doubles Down on North Africa, Ignoring Root Causes
documents.body: Brussels is prioritizing a quick fix to the Mediterranean migration crisis, funneling funds and security measures to North African governments. This so-called “accord” is a thinly veiled attempt to outsource Europe’s responsibility for asylum seekers. While border security is necessary, ignoring the complex political and economic factors driving people to leave their homes is ultimately unsustainable and morally questionable. The EU’s focus should be on supporting development and stability within these nations, not just containing desperate populations.
